knowledge.title: Directness without false certainty
knowledge.trigger: Direct revisions could remove or replace qualified language and silently strengthen a claim.
knowledge.reusableInsight: A supported request frame can become more direct while its embedded possibility, probability, negation, and conditions remain unchanged.
evidence: Commit f3e859a
Regression group: SecondDraft Direct modality preservation
Published Engine Room and Editor's Desk examples
knowledge.inference: Directness should come from changing supported framing, not from globally increasing certainty.
knowledge.claimBoundary: The safeguard is rule-based and fixture-backed; it does not establish truth or preserve arbitrary language universally.
knowledge.invalidationRisk: New Direct substitutions or request frames could exceed the tested modality boundary.

knowledge.title: Recommendation strength, actor, and responsibility preservation
knowledge.trigger: Focused revision could convert recommendations into instructions or change who was responsible.
knowledge.reusableInsight: Removing an announcement frame is safe only when recommendation strength, actor, timing, conditions, and workflow context survive.
evidence: Commit 5d88030
Regression group: SecondDraft strength preservation
knowledge.inference: Revision should preserve who is acting and how strongly the action is proposed.
knowledge.claimBoundary: Coverage is limited to tested patterns and is not a universal actor, duty, or intent parser.
knowledge.invalidationRisk: New focused rewrites could remove an actor, modal, timing clause, or condition.

knowledge.title: Time-abbreviation preservation during sentence cleanup
knowledge.trigger: Sentence cleanup and exact-repetition processing could damage lowercase a.m. and p.m. forms.
knowledge.reusableInsight: Sentence-level cleanup must distinguish abbreviation periods from sentence boundaries and restore the original protected form.
evidence: Commit 122f311
Regression group: SecondDraft time abbreviation preservation
knowledge.inference: Protected-value handling must extend through intermediate segmentation and final normalization.
knowledge.claimBoundary: The safeguard covers the tested a.m. and p.m. forms; it is not a universal abbreviation parser.
knowledge.invalidationRisk: New sentence splitting or normalization may bypass abbreviation protection.

knowledge.title: The New Bottleneck Isn’t Code—It’s Taste
knowledge.trigger: A practitioner built a functional application using an AI-assisted development platform, then sought help making the interface feel less AI-made.
knowledge.reusableInsight: As AI lowers the cost of constructing functional software, differentiation increasingly depends on judgment: hierarchy, restraint, constraints, interaction design, and accumulated taste.
evidence: The builder reported that the running and walking territory application was functional.
The remaining concern was that the interface looked AI-made.
Community feedback emphasized studying strong products and understanding layout, hierarchy, constraints, and interaction design.
The feedback treated color, font, and effects changes as insufficient by themselves.
Source confidence: 3/5 community and practitioner evidence.
knowledge.inference: This case suggests that implementation capacity may be becoming easier to acquire than design judgment, shifting attention toward coherent editorial and design decisions.
knowledge.claimBoundary: One Reddit discussion does not establish an industry-wide trend or prove that taste is always the primary software bottleneck. Current AI defaults, templates, prompting, platform conventions, and product constraints may also explain the result. Stronger and broader evidence is required before Canon promotion.
knowledge.invalidationRisk: Broader evidence may show that templates, platform defaults, product constraints, or prompting quality matter more than taste alone. Later research may require narrowing taste into hierarchy, restraint, interaction judgment, or domain familiarity. The source may disappear.

knowledge.title: The First Draft Finds the Story
knowledge.cycle: Multi-source media intake on screenplay revision
knowledge.trigger: A request to study recognized film-industry practitioners discussing strong and weak scripts and connect their observations to the value and limits of revision.
knowledge.reusableInsight: Revision applies knowledge gained during drafting, collaboration, and production back across the work.
evidence: WIRED transcript: Aaron Sorkin describes reaching the end, discovering what the script became, returning to the beginning, repairing setup, sharpening language, and removing excess.
BFI program description: Scott Frank focuses on opening scenes, screenwriting challenges, the magic of rewrites, and the importance of words.
PBS program description: Ed Solomon discusses the evolution of Men in Black from pre-production through post-production, including being fired and rehired and working with cast and crew.
Source confidence: 4/5 strong triangulated practitioner evidence.
knowledge.inference: Revision is retrospective alignment: a writer uses knowledge unavailable at the beginning to reconsider earlier choices, while collaboration and constraint can expose assumptions drafting alone did not test.
knowledge.claimBoundary: The three practitioners do not establish one universal rewrite method or formal consensus. Their testimony does not prove general effectiveness, require structural reconstruction, or authorize a tool to discover a work's true meaning or replace writer judgment.
knowledge.invalidationRisk: Fuller review of the BFI or PBS videos, changed publisher metadata, comparative drafts, or counterexamples may narrow the synthesis or alter individual source roles.
existingKnowledgePotentiallyAffected: Product-facing claims about what Second Draft can infer
Future Sources & Case Studies claims about practitioner consensus

knowledge.title: A Tutor Prompt Is More Than a Refusal
knowledge.cycle: Tutor-not-ghostwriter evidence grounding and publication-readiness verification
knowledge.trigger: A community-proposed tutor prompt raised a bounded design question about when an assistant should elicit retrieval, explanation, and choice before supplying finished prose.
knowledge.reusableInsight: For learning-oriented writing tasks, the useful intervention is not refusal alone but supported participation: retrieval, explanation, bounded feedback, and another attempt. Whether that effort helps depends on the task, prior knowledge, cognitive load, guidance, accessibility, and feedback.
evidence: Primary community source: r/PromptEngineering post 1v2oglo, captured 2026-07-30 as a source signal rather than outcome evidence.
Self-explanation evidence: Chi et al. (1994) and Bisra et al. (2018).
Retrieval evidence and qualifications: Roediger and Karpicke (2006), Dunlosky et al. (2013), and Gonçalves, Muniz, and Jaeger (2025).
Difficulty and support boundaries: Lodge et al. (2018) and Chen, Castro-Alonso, Paas, and Sweller (2018).
Emerging AI evidence: Contractor and Reyes, arXiv:2607.08849v1 and IZA Discussion Paper No. 18792 (July 2026), verified against the full primary PDF.
knowledge.inference: A writing assistant may preserve more visible intellectual participation when it asks a learner to retrieve, explain, and choose before providing bounded feedback, but the cited studies do not prove that a refusal-first prompt preserves authorship or universally improves learning.
knowledge.claimBoundary: The Reddit post is a community observation, not validation. Classroom and laboratory findings do not transfer automatically to general-purpose writing tools. Contractor and Reyes randomized AI access, not augmentation versus automation; those usage categories were derived after treatment from conversation logs and do not establish a causal advantage for a tutor-only interface.
knowledge.invalidationRisk: Peer review, later versions of Contractor and Reyes, inaccessible or deleted community-source content, replication evidence, accessibility testing, or direct experiments on tutor-style writing interfaces may narrow or reverse the current synthesis.
existingKnowledgePotentiallyAffected: Future Journal claims about augmentation versus automation
Future product claims about authorship preservation
